title: Stratospheric and Tropospheric Vortex Disruptions and Extreme Events in the Northern Hemisphere in 2026: Mechanisms at Play
content: Current theories attribute a decisive role in the formation of extreme events to the meanders formed by jet streams when they slow down. These meanders are thought to foster the de-velopment of persistent atmospheric blocking patterns, impeding the westerly flow that carries mild oceanic air while channeling extremely cold, dense Arctic air toward mid-latitudes. It is as if, once released from the "barrier" holding it back, polar air rapidly flows southward via advection. Here, we propose complementing this intuitive, simplify-ing, and holistic approach. The method relies on both the resonant forcing of tropospheric multifrequency Rossby waves into harmonic modes and a joint analysis of the time lag between geostrophic wind velocity anomalies at the tropopause and geopotential height anomalies at the mid-tropopause. This analysis utilizes cross-wavelet coherence and phase—relative to a common reference—for geostrophic wind velocity and geopotential height within the 8.6–17.1-day and 17.1–34.2-day period bands that govern blocking pro-cesses. By establishing causal links, the study demonstrates the importance of geostrophic wind velocity anomalies—associated with polar vortices and polar jet streams—in the formation of mid-latitude geopotential height anomalies. The findings reveal that the his-toric cold wave striking North America in January and February 2026—resulting from a split in the stratospheric polar vortex—was driven by a vast annular high-pressure system acting as an anticyclone. Similarly, the successive heatwaves experienced by Europe dur-ing the summer of 2026 resulted from coupled eddy systems arising from the interaction between geostrophic winds associated, on the one hand, with a southward-shifted lobe of the tropospheric polar vortex and, on the other, with the displaced polar jet stream.
